title: Unrestricted strict-henselization stalk formula
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $F$ be an abelian etale sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $S_{(\bar x)}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $p:X\times_S S_{(\bar x)}\to X$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $q\geq0$, the canonical restriction map $(R^q f_*F)_{\bar x}\to H^q((X\times_S S_{(\bar x)})_{\mathrm{Et}},p^{-1}F)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf], $R^qf_*F$ is the sheafification of the presheaf $V\mapsto H^q(X\times_SV,F|)$ on $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Taking the geometric stalk and using [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-geometric-stalk] identifies $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar x}$ with the filtered colimit of these cohomology groups over pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar x$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 proof, first displayed equality

proof.text: By [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal], the colimit may be restricted to affine pointed neighbourhoods $V$. Their inverse limit is $S_{(\bar x)}$ by [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and [lemma-weil-pbc-fibre-product-limit] identifies $X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}$ with the inverse limit of $X\times_SV$. The hypotheses that $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated make all these base changes quasi-compact and quasi-separated, while maps between affine neighbourhoods give affine transition maps.

Choose an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(V_0,\bar v_0)$ and restrict to the cofinal subsystem of affine pointed neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ equipped with a map to $(V_0,\bar v_0)$; it is cofiltered and has the same limits and colimits (Step 2). Put $T=X\times_SV_0$. The schemes $X\times_SV$ form a cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated $T$-schemes with affine transition maps (Step 2) and limit $X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-etale-cohomology-limit] to this system and to $K=F|_{X\times_SV_0}$ placed in degree $0$. Elementary: by [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] the derived inverse image of a complex concentrated in degree $0$ is the termwise inverse image, again concentrated in degree $0$, and the inverse image of $F|_{X\times_SV_0}$ along $X\times_SV\to X\times_SV_0$ is $F|_{X\times_SV}$ and along $X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}\to X\times_SV_0$ is $p^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]; the degree-$q$ cohomology of a sheaf in degree $0$ is its $H^q$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Hence the lemma identifies the filtered colimit in Step 1 with $H^q((X\times_SS_{(\bar x)})_{\mathrm{Et}},p^{-1}F)$. The identifications are induced by restriction along the projections, so their composite is the canonical restriction map in the statement.
